definition: Anathema means something or someone utterly detested and rejected.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word anathema. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know anathema should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Instant coffee is anathema to my grandfather, who roasts his own beans and grinds them by hand before dawn.
An irritant merely chafes and can be lived with — nowhere near anathema, which names a thing utterly rejected.
An abomination disgusts, but it stops short of anathema, which adds banishment: the thing is not only loathed but cast out entirely.

A curse is a thing formally damned, with ritual or a church behind the damning — anathema's church-flavored cousin. Anathema began the same way but now lives in everyday prose: whatever a person or group utterly rejects on principle is anathema to them, no ceremony required.

A taboo is forbidden by rule or custom — the community's shared law does the rejecting, and breaking it invites punishment. Anathema is personal: the rejection comes from a person or group's own principles, and it holds even when no rule forbids the thing. Instant coffee breaks no law, yet it is anathema to some.
